title: Bobara brings a weather-watching capybara to your iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch
summary: Somewhere along the way we agreed that capybaras are the most relaxed animals going, and I’ve never seen a good reason to argue. Some Japanese zoos even run them hot baths in winter. They just sit in there, eyes half shut, while the rest of the world carries on without them. Bobara puts one of them in your pocket, and it’s on its way to the App Store next month. It’s a small app about Momo, a capybara who lives in an onsen across your iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch, with an Apple TV version that fills the big screen and reads his collection over iCloud. ... [MORE]

title: Duskroot is a Stardew Valley-style game that's just had a big update on mobile
summary: It's funny that after talking about Thrifty Business earlier today, we have another sort-of-management sim to talk about. Duskroot, a farming sim that draws heavy inspiration from the likes of Stardew Valley, is one to take a look at if the genre is your thing. Especially with a major new update now available! The latest update to Duskroot expands the scope of its farm simulation even further by introducing animals and orchards. Whether it's planting trees for apples or waiting for milk (and truffles from your trusty pig), you'll find that there are all-new ways to make money and expand your farming enterprise. ... [MORE]

title: Thrifty Business has you running your own 90s-inspired thrift store, coming soon to mobile
summary: We've had farms, we've had supermarkets, and now the latest cosy simulator to arrive on mobile puts you in the role of a charity shop owner! Sorry, thrift shop owner, as there's a difference, believe it or not. But in Thrifty Business the objective is the same as it always is: make money and keep your customers happy. Coming to iOS and Android on November 10th, retailing for $7.99 from Spellgarden Games, Thrifty Business is a 90s-inspired management sim that sees you bringing pre-loved items to the masses. With your own pastel-coated thrift shop, you'll lay out your displays and discover new and unusual items to pass on to your customers. ... [MORE]

title: Titanium Court is a quirky mix of match-3 with grid-based strategy, and it's all a bit strange in a good way
summary: Time to put on your thinking cap and get your media literacy degree, because there's a surreal new game coming to mobile this month. AP Thomson's wacky, strange and esoteric grid-based strategy, puzzler, mystery, point-and-click thing Titanium Court lands on mobile October 29th! And it's somehow easier to describe what it isn't rather than what it is, but I'll try anyway. Titanium Court is made intentionally difficult to describe, but at its core seems to be a combination of match-three, roguelike and real-time strategy where you manipulate the terrain of a world to gather resources, recruit soldiers and destroy your enemy. Of course, in between all that will be interludes, mysteries and oddities that suggest something more happening beneath the surface. ... [MORE]

title: Beyond Words puts a Balatro-style spin on Scrabble, now on iOS
summary: It would seem that the constantly growing subgenre of Balatro-like games isn't slowing anytime soon. Beyond Words takes yet another tabletop classic and puts a roguelike spin on it. But with a pedigree including two of the minds behind hits such as GoldenEye 64 and TimeSplitters, it's well worth a look! In case you hadn't already guessed, Beyond Words: A Word Roguelike takes the classic tabletop pastime of Scrabble and adds in many of the elements Balatro helped popularise. You'll be tasked with making longer and more complex words, meeting ever higher score requirements, and making use of modifiers and upgrades to continue growing your multiplier! ... [MORE]

title: Walk the Frog, the Post-it note puzzler, launches for iOS and Android
summary: Walk the Frog, the Post-it Note puzzler from the developer of the same name, is out now on iOS and Android. Seeing you guiding the humble Froggog back home in time to meet up with his friend Buddy and attend the Froggapalooza festival. Available for $6.99, it's a mix of puzzler, adventure book and cute critter capers. Okay, but what do I actually mean when I say that it's a Post-it note puzzler? Well, the core gameplay of Walk The Frog is all about getting Froggo home, and to do that you'll need to lay out his path, which means rearranging the sticky notes covered with artwork and mapping out the correct route through each level! ... summary: Everybody loves animals, right? And if you're a Farmville 2: Country Escape player, I'd bet money on the fact that caring for animals is a big thing for you. title: Royal Cooking serves up 50 million downloads without a royal in sight
summary: Every town seems to have a restaurant called the Royal something, and I’d bet very few of them have ever had an actual royal through the door. Royal Cooking keeps that tradition going nicely. No palace kitchen, no monarch sending the soup back, just a lot of restaurants and hungry customers, and by now more than 50 million downloads of it. If you’ve run a kitchen in any time management sim before, Matryoshka Games won’t surprise you much. Orders come in, you cook and serve them, and the coins go back into better equipment and nicer ingredients so the next shift runs a bit quicker than the last one. You can shuffle the kitchen layout around as well, to get the stations where you want them before the queues start backing up. ... [MORE]

title: Fishing Inc turns waiting for a bite into an incremental upgrade chase
summary: From everything I’ve heard from people who actually do it, fishing is largely sitting about and waiting. Incremental games are much the same, just with a number going up while you wait, so the two were always going to get on. Fishing Inc is the latest to try it, and it’s now open for pre-registration on iOS and Android. BigBonk Studios is developing it, with Snapbreak taking publishing duties. You start off with basic gear and catches that wouldn’t impress anyone, and from there it’s a case of moving on to new spots and finding more species as your kit gets better. Cash from every catch goes back into equipment, plus new abilities, most of which seem to be about catching things faster. ... [MORE]

title: Monopoly Go returns to McDonald’s with free shields and a mountain of dice
summary: McDonald’s has been sticking Monopoly pieces on its packaging since the late 80s, and at this point the two go together about as naturally as fries and salt. So, no great shock that Monopoly Go is back at the counter for a second year, tagging along with the McDonald’s Monopoly promotion in the US. You peel the game piece off eligible packaging and scan it in the McDonald’s app, and that gets you a shot at mobile prizes alongside the usual food ones. You’ll need to have signed up for the promotion in the app first, mind. The big prize is $100,000 towards gold bars, with up to two winners. Below that, 10,000 bundles of 5,300 dice rolls are being handed out. That’s a lot of dice. ... [MORE]

title: Replaced sees the dystopian cyberpunk platformer making its way to Android
summary: It's a bit of a trite observation, but sometimes it really feels as if we're living in a cyberpunk dystopia, just without the cool stuff. Fortunately, if you're hankering for a neon-soaked world to explore, then you're in luck, because 2.5D cinematic platformer Replaced is set to make its way to Android on December 9th! Set in an alternate-universe 1980s America, you play as R.E.A.C.H., an AI that's been unexpectedly placed into a human body. You'll explore the sprawling metropolis of Phoenix City and do battle with the sinister Phoenix Corporation in your typical dour cyberpunk urban hellscape where human life is cheap. ... [MORE]

title: The One Bullet Job is a heist puzzler where you only get one shot. Literally.
summary: We all love a good heist film, like Ocean's Eleven or Mission: Impossible. But translating that into a game has proven surprisingly tricky, even as it's been attempted as far back as the days of tabletop gaming. Now, The One Bullet Job is the latest to try and make you feel like a master thief when it arrives on Android October 16th. If you hadn't already guessed, One Bullet Job's core gimmick is right in the title. You play a heister whose objective is to navigate the grid, gather cash, avoid guards, and, if necessary, take them out before making your escape. And, of course, you have only one bullet to do so. ... [MORE]
